threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' when it’s just the London Overground. Locals know it’s a vibe, not just a route.
Last night on the 196, a guy was loudly singing opera. No one joined in, but we all pretended it was normal. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy fixing his bike in front of a café, chatting with the barista over pastries. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night Kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery, where the walls are covered in ever-changing street art.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission if they can spot the difference between taco trucks on 24th and 26th without breaking a sweat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, I saw a guy in a full tuxedo jump on the 14, only to pull out a saxophone and start playing. Typical Mission magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars serve vermut on tap. Try finding one that does outside Gràcia; it’s like searching for needles in haystacks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the sheer number of ferreteries—who knew you’d need a hardware store for every neighborhood?

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of just 'the Overground' for your local journeys. Everyone here knows the real magic is above ground.
Caught a guy singing opera at the back of the 196 last night. Only in Brixton does that feel normal—everyone joined in for a verse.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids playing football in the street, their laughter mixing with the sound of the nearby kebab shop’s grill. That was Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a silent disco in a former factory, where the beats blend with the sound of the Spree — surreal but so local.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how easily they navigate around BART delays—while newcomers just stare at the screen like it’ll start moving on its own.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The Muni bus rolled up with a guy playing a saxophone out front, and between stops, he even took requests. Classic San Francisco hustle.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the flower shops sell the same stuff, but locals know the ones with unique plants are hidden in backstreets like Carrer de Verdi.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they order 'tapas' as if it's a single dish. Locals know it's a sharing experience, not a meal.
